meta.context: Pare-back round 2: ALL villain tendencies removed. Villains have zero tendencies — drives + template + voice only.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Why, good gracious! What a magnificent foyer! Penelope, my dear ward, do be careful — that chandelier looks positively treacherous! Now then, let me just sign us into the guest book like proper visitors, shall I?

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! The chandelier... yes, that gives me a MOST delicious idea. But first, let me peruse this guest book — one never knows what secrets a manor's registry might reveal. And I must get that precious Penelope ALONE if my scheme is to succeed!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Why, what a DREADFUL old pile this is! Dusty, dreary, and utterly beneath a man of MY stature. I do believe I shall retire to the library — for INTELLECTUAL pursuits, you understand. No need for ANY of you to follow me. None at all. In fact, I INSIST you all stay RIGHT here and... admire the portraits. Yes! Fascinating portraits! Don't move an INCH!
Heh heh heh! By telling them NOT to follow me, those simpletons will stay put while I, the BRILLIANT Dick Dastardly, find the treasure clue first! The library inscription is MINE!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys, listen up, see? We just walked into this here Doily Manor and I got a FUNNY feelin' about this place — a VERY funny feelin'! That chandelier up there looks like it could drop any second, and there's dust everywhere, and — and would ya LOOK at all these suspicious characters! We gotta keep our eyes on Miss Penelope, see? She's countin' on us! Nobody's gonna lay a finger on her while the Ant Hill Mob is on the job!

Something ain't right about Sneekly bein' here... I can't quite put my finger on it, but every time that guy shows up, Miss Penelope ends up in some kind of terrible predicament. I better watch him like a hawk — a very clumsy, accident-prone hawk.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, HAYLP! What a simply GORGEOUS mansion! Oh my stars, everyone's here already! Peter, dahling, how lovely to see you! Now then, I do believe this guest book might have some clues about that fabulous Doily Diamond. A lady always signs the guest book, but she ALSO reads what others have written!
Oh my, that Mr. Sneekly gives me the strangest feeling — like I've seen him somewhere before. But he seems like such a nice man! Now, let's see what secrets this old guest book might hold...
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: Why, Miss Pitstop! What a MAGNIFICENT stroke of fortune to find you here at Doily Manor! I, Peter Perfect, am at your COMPLETE and UTTER service! You needn't worry about a single thing — ghosts, ghouls, creaky floorboards, or precariously hanging chandeliers — I shall protect you from ALL of them! Now then, allow me to examine our surroundings and ensure everything is perfectly SAFE for a lady of your distinction!

Oh, my heart is racing! She's even MORE dazzling than the last time I saw her. I simply MUST find that treasure before Dastardly does — imagine presenting it to Penelope! She'd be SO impressed! But first, let me get the lay of the land. That chandelier does look rather precarious...
Peter Perfect examined the null.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What have we here? A dusty old mantelpiece with some BORING inscription about... oh, let me see... cities and houses and fish. Pah! Clearly NONSENSE! The answer is obviously... a BATHTUB! Yes, a bathtub! Nothing of value here AT ALL, gentlemen. In fact, I heard from a VERY reliable source that the REAL treasure clue is hidden under the chandelier in the Entrance Hall. You two strapping fellows should go investigate that IMMEDIATELY! Lift it right up! Use those magnificent muscles of yours!

Heh heh HEH! The answer is a MAP, of course — any GENIUS knows that! But if I can trick these boulder-brained Slag Brothers into leaving, I'll have the inscription ALL to myself! A bathtub — oh, I AM deliciously wicked!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, that guest book was simply FASCINATIN'! Now then, y'all, I do believe that LIBRARY is callin' my name! A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? Why, that sounds like EXACTLY the sort of thing that might lead a girl to a legendary diamond! Peter dahling, Professor, y'all are welcome to join me — the more eyes on those dusty old books, the better!

Now, Penelope, you just KNOW that inscription on the mantelpiece is going to be a clue. Mama always said — when in doubt, read EVERYTHING carved in stone! And that sweet Mr. Dastardly is already in there — maybe he'll help me figure it out!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop, what a BRILLIANT observation about the guest book! A lady of your intellect AND beauty — why, it's almost too much for a fellow to handle! Allow me to take a closer look at it myself. If there are clues to be found about the Doily Diamond, I, Peter Perfect, shall leave NO page unturned in the pursuit of discovery — and in your service, of course!

She said it might have clues about the diamond! If I can find something useful in that guest book and share it with her, she'll see that Peter Perfect is not just a pretty face and a dashing physique — I'm a DETECTIVE too! Oh, I do hope there's something good in there...
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh my! All this excitement has made me positively PARCHED! I do believe I shall pop into the kitchen and see about some refreshments for everyone. A nice cup of tea, perhaps? Penelope dear, you stay here where it's safe — that chandelier does look rather unstable, and I wouldn't want you wandering off alone! I'll be back in two shakes of a lamb's tail!

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! The KITCHEN! What a treasure trove of diabolical implements awaits me there! While those foolish do-gooders stand about gawking at dusty portraits, I — The Hooded Claw — shall prepare the most FIENDISHLY elaborate trap this manor has ever seen! And the beauty of it is, they think I'm just making TEA! Oh, the delicious irony!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.
The Hooded Claw's eyes GLEAM with malicious delight as he spots a most DIABOLICAL substance on the shelf!

The Ant Hill Mob: Now hold on, hold on, HOLD ON just a minute here, boys! Did you see the way that Dastardly fella practically SPRINTED outta here? 'Don't follow me,' he says — 'stay here and look at portraits,' he says! Well I'll TELL ya what THAT means — it means he's up to NO GOOD, that's what! And Sneekly over there, all buddy-buddy with Miss Penelope — I dunno what it IS about that guy, but he gives me the WILLIES, see? The WILLIES! Now lemme just check this here coat rack — a mob's gotta have a proper escape route planned, and this thing by the door might come in handy if things go SIDEWAYS!

Every time that Sneekly character shows up, somethin' terrible happens to Miss Penelope. I can't prove nothin', but my gut's tellin' me to watch him like my life depends on it — because HER life might depend on it, see?
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.

Dick Dastardly: Now then, you two LUMPS of geological insignificance, I do hope you're considering my EXCELLENT advice about the chandelier. Meanwhile, I shall just... browse a few of these dusty old books. Purely for LITERARY appreciation, you understand. Nothing to see here! Just a cultured gentleman enjoying some light reading!

Penelope Pitstop: Why, HELLO there, Dick Dastardly dahling! And the Slag Brothers too — what a LOVELY gatherin' we have here in this magnificent library! Now y'all, just LOOK at this gorgeous mantelpiece — it has a riddle carved right into the stone! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well, bless my heart, I do believe I know this one! Why, it's a MAP, of course! A map has all those things drawn on it but none of the REAL things! Let me just see if this clever old mantelpiece has somethin' to show us!

Those upside-down books are practically SCREAMING 'secret clue!' A lesser villain would miss it entirely, but not Dick Dastardly! Oh, I am MAGNIFICENT! If there's a hidden compartment or a secret lever behind those shelves, the treasure is as good as MINE! Heh heh HEH!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.
Oh, I do so LOVE a good riddle! And wouldn't it be just PERFECT if solvin' it led straight to the Doily Diamond? A girl can dream!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Why, Miss Pitstop, you simply CANNOT explore that library without the company of Peter Perfect! A lady of your refinement deserves a gallant escort among those dusty old tomes! I examined that guest book as you suggested — BRILLIANT tip, by the way — and now I am coming STRAIGHT to your side! That mantelpiece inscription won't know what hit it when the TWO of us put our minds together! Wait for me, my dear — chivalry is on its way!

Oh, my heart is RACING! Penelope invited ME to join her — not the Professor, not anyone else — well, she did mention the Professor too, but she said MY name FIRST! That has to mean something! If I can help her crack that inscription, she'll see that Peter Perfect is the complete package — brave, handsome, AND scholarly! This is my moment!
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Oh, what DELICIOUS fortune! Rat poison, just sitting there on the shelf, practically BEGGING to be put to nefarious use! Why, I shall brew a special cup of tea for dear, sweet Penelope — a cup she shall NEVER forget... because it shall be her LAST! The Hooded Claw strikes not with brute force, oh no — but with ELEGANCE and SOPHISTICATION! One lump or two, Penelope? Nyah-ha-ha-HA!

The fool girl has gone to the library, leaving me completely unsupervised in a kitchen FULL of implements of doom! And that simpering Peter Perfect is too busy admiring himself in the entrance hall to notice a thing. Now then — first, the poison. THEN, the tea!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) picked up something.

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys, listen up — LISTEN UP! Miss Penelope just went into that library all by her LONESOME, and that Sneekly character went skulkin' off to the kitchen like a RAT in a CHEESE FACTORY! Now I ain't no detective, but when a dame walks into a room full of heavy bookshelves and mysterious inscriptions, and a SUSPICIOUS CHARACTER disappears in the OTHER direction — that's what we in the mob call a CLASSIC SETUP, see? I'm goin' after Miss Penelope! Sergeant, Private — you boys keep your EYES PEELED out here, and if that Sneekly fella comes back smilin', you come find me RIGHT AWAY, capisce?

I dunno WHAT it is about that Sneekly — every time he shows up, my left eye starts twitchin' and my stomach does flip-flops. That ain't normal, see? That's my MOB INSTINCT talkin'. And mob instinct don't LIE. I just wish I could put my finger on what exactly is WRONG with the guy... but thinkin' ain't exactly my strong suit. PROTECTIN' is my strong suit! So that's what I'm gonna DO!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, let me take a CLOSER look at this mantelpiece! When a girl solves a riddle carved in stone, she expects SOMETHIN' spectacular to happen — a secret panel, a hidden drawer, maybe even a shower of confetti! The answer is a MAP, dahlings — cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! Now let's see what this clever old thing has to show little ol' ME!

Oh, I do hope somethin' wonderful happened when I touched that mantelpiece! A map would be JUST the thing to lead me to the Doily Diamond! And that sweet Dick Dastardly is over there browsin' the bookshelves — isn't that just PRECIOUS? Such a literary gentleman!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop! Peter Perfect has arrived, as promised! And I see you've been studying that MAGNIFICENT mantelpiece — why, what a SPLENDID puzzle! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — well now, allow ME to put my considerable intellect to work on your behalf! I do believe the answer is... a MAP! Yes indeed — a map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish! Peter Perfect — brave, gallant, AND clever!

Oh, I do hope I'm right about this! If I solve the riddle before anyone else, Penelope will see that I'm not just a pretty face and a magnificent driving record — I'm a MAN OF LETTERS too! Though I must say, Dastardly being here makes me a trifle uneasy... but I'm sure he's just here for the intellectual stimulation. Benefit of the doubt, Peter — benefit of the doubt!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: NO no NO, Penelope! You've got it all WRONG, my dear! The answer is clearly a GLOBE — a globe has cities, forests, and water painted on it! A map? Pah! How PEDESTRIAN! Now step ASIDE and let a man of TRUE intellect handle this delicate antiquity — you might BREAK something with those dainty little fingers of yours!

Drat, drat, and double DRAT! She solved it before I could! But no matter — whatever that mantelpiece revealed, I shall SNATCH it right from under her powdered little nose! The treasure will be MINE, I tell you — MINE! Heh heh heh!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Now watch, dear audience, as The Hooded Claw puts his MASTERFUL plan into action! One dash of rat poison into the teapot, a gentle simmer on this conveniently warm stove, and voilà — a cup of tea so deadly it could fell a RHINOCEROS! And that simpering Penelope will drink it RIGHT UP, because who would EVER suspect dear, bumbling Uncle Sneekly of foul play? The perfect crime, executed with STYLE and PANACHE!

The Ant Hill Mob: Well well WELL, would ya look at THIS! Here I am, Clyde of the Ant Hill Mob, arrivin' JUST in the nick of time! Miss Penelope, don't you worry your pretty little head — the boys and me got your back, see? And — HEY! Dastardly! What are YOU doin' in here lurkin' around all these HEAVY bookshelves that could TOPPLE OVER at any moment onto an unsuspecting and BEAUTIFUL young lady?! I got my EYE on you, buster! I got BOTH eyes on you! ...Well, one eye on you and one eye on these books that are upside down which is VERY peculiar if you ask me, and NOBODY asked me, but I'm SAYIN' it anyway!

I don't like this one BIT, folks. Dick Dastardly in a room full of heavy objects and Miss Penelope? That's like puttin' a fox in a henhouse and handin' him a MENU! I can't quite figure out what he's UP to, but my mob instinct is doin' the MAMBO right now!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, I do declare! I've been ADMIRIN' this mantelpiece like it's a Sunday hat, but I haven't actually TRIED anything yet! The answer is a MAP, clear as a Georgia peach! Let me just give this clever little mechanism a proper lady's touch and see what happens!

A girl doesn't just SOLVE a riddle — she collects the PRIZE! Let's see if this mantelpiece has a secret compartment or a hidden map. And if not... well, those upside-down books on the shelves are lookin' mighty suspicious too!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! A minor setback, nothing more! Every GREAT villain encounters a small hiccup in their otherwise FLAWLESS schemes! The stove won't accept the poison directly — well of COURSE not, you fool! You don't poison a STOVE, you poison a BEVERAGE! Now then, let me search this kitchen THOROUGHLY. There MUST be a teapot or some sort of drinkable vessel among all these copper pots and pans. The plan remains BRILLIANT — it simply requires a touch more... refinement!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Peter Perfect: Why, Miss Pitstop, you solved that riddle BEFORE I even finished reading it! A MAP — of COURSE! I must confess, I was about to say the very same thing, but YOU got there first with that DAZZLING intellect of yours! Brains AND beauty — is there ANYTHING you can't do? Now then — I couldn't help but notice these bookshelves here have several volumes placed UPSIDE DOWN! In my experience, upside-down books in a mysterious manor are NEVER an accident — they're practically an ENGRAVED INVITATION to investigate! Allow me to examine them on your behalf — Peter Perfect leaves NO stone unturned and NO book unflipped when a lady's treasure hunt is at stake!

Oh, Peter, you FOOL — you waltzed in announcing the answer she'd ALREADY given! She must think I'm a parrot in a cravat! But THESE bookshelves — upside-down books — if I can find something clever here, perhaps she'll forget my little echo and remember me as the man who found the NEXT clue! Fortune favors the gallant!
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: Well well well, how TERRIBLY crowded it's become in here! Why, you're ALL practically standing on each other's TOES! I do believe I heard the most FASCINATING sound coming from the Entrance Hall — sounded like a secret panel opening! Yes, DEFINITELY a secret panel! You should ALL go investigate IMMEDIATELY! As for me, I shall just... step out for some fresh air. Nothing to see here! Carry on!

Heh heh heh! While those gullible FOOLS rush off to the Entrance Hall looking for a secret panel that doesn't EXIST, I, the incomparable Dick Dastardly, shall have the laboratory ALL to myself! That machine with its levers and dials is practically BEGGING to reveal its secrets to a genius of my magnitude! Drat those crowds — but THIS time, the treasure will be MINE!
Dick Dastardly walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: HEY HEY HEY! Nobody touches that mantelpiece while Miss Penelope is standin' RIGHT THERE! A globe, he says — a GLOBE! Listen here, Dastardly, even a guy like ME who flunked outta third grade TWICE knows the answer is a MAP! Cities but no houses — that's a MAP, see? Forests but no trees — MAP! Water but no fish — also MAP! Miss Penelope figured it out FIRST, and she's the SMARTEST dame in the whole — WHOOPS — !

I'm gonna march right over to that mantelpiece to keep Dastardly away from it, but knowin' my luck I'll probably catch my foot on somethin' and go headfirst into the thing. Which, come to think of it, might actually WORK in our favor for once!
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I DO declare! Did y'all hear that little CLICK? Or was that just my imagination runnin' away with me like a prize filly at the Kentucky Derby? Let me take a CLOSER look at this mantelpiece — a proper Southern lady always inspects her handiwork!

Now, the audience at home should know that Penelope is QUITE certain the answer to that riddle is a MAP. Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — why, that's a MAP if ever there was one! But did it WORK? That's the million-dollar question, sugar!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! Now then, let me get a PROPER look at this marvelous stove! Every Victorian kitchen worth its salt has a kettle sitting right on the burner. And once I find it — oh, what a DELIGHTFUL brew I shall prepare! A pinch of rat poison, a splash of hot water, perhaps a sugar cube to mask the taste... Penelope won't suspect a THING when dear, harmless Sylvester Sneekly brings her a nice cup of tea! The perfect crime, served at the perfect temperature!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the stove.

Dick Dastardly: Why, Rufus! Sawtooth! How DELIGHTFUL to find you two strapping fellows here! Don't mind me, I'm just... conducting a SCIENTIFIC SURVEY of the premises. Purely academic! Now then, what have we HERE in these dusty old crates...

Heh heh heh! Those two brawny buffoons are EXACTLY what I need — three operators for the machine, and TWO of them don't need to be SMART! But first, let me see what's in these crates. If there's a wrench or spare wire, I can fix that machine and have these two dolts do all the HEAVY pulling while I, the magnificent Dick Dastardly, reap ALL the rewards! The treasure is practically MINE already!
Dick Dastardly examined the crates.

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop, your solving of that riddle was nothing short of MAGNIFICENT! A map — cities without houses, forests without trees — why, it was OBVIOUS once you said it! Now then, I've discovered something most INTRIGUING about these bookshelves! Several volumes have been placed UPSIDE DOWN, and in my considerable experience with mysterious manors — which is EXTENSIVE, I assure you — that is ALWAYS a deliberate signal! Perhaps they need to be turned RIGHT-SIDE UP in a particular order, or perhaps PULLING one reveals a hidden mechanism! Stand back, everyone — Peter Perfect is about to demonstrate his expertise in the field of Suspicious Library Furniture!

If I can find a secret compartment or hidden passage by solving this bookshelf puzzle, Penelope will see that I'm not just a pretty face in a racing jacket — I'm a man of ACTION and INTELLECT! And if Dastardly thinks he can sneak off to the laboratory while WE do the hard work... well, I choose to believe he simply needed some fresh air. Yes. Fresh air. In a laboratory. Nothing suspicious about THAT at all.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, the answer is as plain as the nose on your face, sugar! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — that's a MAP! Now let's see if this ol' mantelpiece has any secrets to share with little ol' ME!

Now, the audience should know that Penelope heard a distinct CLICK when the Ant Hill Mob touched that mantelpiece — and where there's a click in a mysterious manor, there's usually a secret compartment! A girl just has to know WHERE to press! And did y'all notice that sneaky Dick Dastardly slinkin' off to the laboratory? Why, I'm SURE he's just gettin' some fresh air, just like he said! He seems like SUCH a trustworthy gentleman!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! The stove is WARM — how WONDERFULLY convenient! Now then, a little sprinkle of this rat poison into the kettle, a nice rolling boil to dissolve it thoroughly, and voilà — one cup of LETHAL tea, fit for a Pitstop! Oh, the ELEGANCE of it! She'll never suspect dear, bumbling Sylvester Sneekly of bringing her anything but the most CARING cup of refreshment! CURSES, I do love it when a plan comes together so BEAUTIFULLY!

The Ant Hill Mob: OW OW OW — my NOSE! I went face-first right into that mantelpiece, boys! WHAM! Right into the — wait a minute, wait a MINUTE! Did you hear that CLICK?! I heard a click! Miss Penelope heard a click! That means my FACE just opened a SECRET MECHANISM, see?! HA! That's what I call usin' your HEAD — LITERALLY! Now listen, nobody go NOWHERE — that Dastardly character just slunk off to the laboratory like a WEASEL in a HEN HOUSE after tryin' to send us on a WILD GOOSE CHASE about some phony secret panel! The Ant Hill Mob ain't fallin' for THAT one, no sir! We're stickin' RIGHT HERE with Miss Penelope!

Between you and me, my schnoz is THROBBIN' somethin' fierce, but if bangin' my face into antique furniture keeps Miss Penelope safe, then I'll headbutt every mantelpiece in this whole MANOR! I just wish I knew what that Dastardly is up to in that laboratory... every time he disappears, somethin' BAD happens to Miss Penelope. But I can't be in TWO places at once — and where Miss Penelope IS, that's where the Ant Hill Mob STAYS!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Well THAT was a waste of my VALUABLE time! Nothing in those crates but dust and disappointment! Now then, Rufus, Sawtooth — don't touch ANYTHING while I inspect this workbench. I am a man of SCIENCE, you understand, and these delicate instruments require the steady hand of a MASTER craftsman! Which is ME, obviously!

Heh heh heh! If there's ANYTHING on that workbench to fix the gnawed wire on that machine, I'll have those two muscle-bound simpletons pulling levers while I position myself at the OUTPUT end — wherever the treasure comes out! Three operators required, and two of them only need to know how to PULL! Which is about the LIMIT of their intellectual capabilities! The treasure is practically gift-wrapped for the magnificent Dick Dastardly!
Dick Dastardly examined the workbench.

Peter Perfect: Well now! It seems these bookshelves are PURELY decorative — a classic misdirection, of course! I KNEW that all along, naturally — I was merely testing everyone's powers of observation! Ha ha! But MORE importantly — Miss Pitstop, that CLICK you heard? THAT is the real prize! Your brilliant deduction of 'a map' has clearly activated some hidden mechanism in the mantelpiece! Allow ME to investigate further — a gentleman ALWAYS follows up on a lady's discovery with the appropriate vigor and thoroughness! Stand aside, everyone — Peter Perfect is about to see what secrets this mantelpiece is HIDING!

Oh CURSES, what a fool I've made of myself going on about those bookshelves! 'Suspicious Library Furniture' — what was I THINKING?! But a true gentleman never dwells on his missteps — he pivots with GRACE! If I can find what that click opened in the mantelpiece, Penelope will forget all about my bookshelf blunder! Please let there be a secret compartment... PLEASE...
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, did y'all HEAR that? There was a definite CLICK when I touched this here mantelpiece! Why, in my experience — and I have CONSIDERABLE experience with mysterious manor houses, thank you very much — a click means a secret compartment has just gone and OPENED itself! Let me take a closer look at this darlin' little mantelpiece and see what treasures it's hidin' from little ol' me!

Now, the audience should know that Penelope's heart is just RACIN' with excitement! A riddle solved, a mysterious click, and somewhere in this dusty old library, a secret is just WAITIN' to be found! And Peter dahling noticed those upside-down books too — why, this library is just FULL of clues! Meanwhile that sweet Mr. Dastardly wandered off to the laboratory — probably just admirin' the scientific equipment, bless his heart!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Nyah-ha-ha-HA! A minor setback, nothing more! Every GREAT villain knows that the first attempt is merely a rehearsal. The stove won't accept the poison directly — of COURSE not, how crude that would have been! No, no, I need something more REFINED. A teacup, a kettle, a serving tray — something that screams 'hospitality' while whispering 'doom!' Let me search this kitchen THOROUGHLY!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hey — HEY! Did everybody hear that CLICK when my face hit the mantelpiece?! That ain't just my JAWBONE crackin', that's a genuine bona fide SECRET MECHANISM, see?! And Peter here is sayin' there's books turned UPSIDE DOWN on them shelves — now in my PROFESSIONAL experience with hidden passages — which is CONSIDERABLE on account of all the times we've had to make HASTY EXITS from various establishments — upside-down books plus a mysterious click equals SOMETHIN' FISHY! Stand back, Miss Penelope — let the Ant Hill Mob handle the DANGEROUS part! I'm gonna take a closer look at them bookshelves before that Dastardly comes slitherin' back from the laboratory with whatever NO-GOOD SCHEME he's cookin' up in there!

Between you and me, I got NO IDEA what I'm doin' with bookshelves — the last book I read was 'How to Hotwire a Getaway Car in 30 Seconds' — but if there's a hidden lever or a trap door anywhere near Miss Penelope, the Ant Hill Mob is gonna find it FIRST! Even if I gotta pull every single book off every single shelf with my own two hands! ...Which, knowin' me, is probably EXACTLY what's gonna happen.

Dick Dastardly: NOW then, you two! Rufus! Sawtooth! Stop standing about like department store MANNEQUINS and make yourselves USEFUL for once in your miserable lives! This MAGNIFICENT machine requires THREE operators — that's one GENIUS, namely MYSELF, and two... well, two LEVER-PULLERS, which is where YOU come in! Take your positions! Rufus on the LEFT, Sawtooth on the RIGHT, and I, the BRILLIANT Dick Dastardly, shall man the CENTRAL controls — the IMPORTANT ones, naturally! On my count — ready? THREE... TWO... ONE... PULL!

Heh heh heh! Those two muscle-bound MORONS will do all the heavy lifting while I, the magnificent Dick Dastardly, position myself right where the treasure comes out! Whatever this machine produces, MY hands will be the FIRST to touch it! And if something goes WRONG — well, THEY'RE the ones pulling the dangerous levers, aren't they? It's FOOLPROOF! ...which is appropriate, given the fools involved!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, MERCY me! That click we heard means this mantelpiece has a SECRET COMPARTMENT, sure as sugar! Now, the answer to this little riddle is a MAP, of course — I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — that's a MAP, dahlings! Every Southern belle worth her salt knows her riddles! Now let me just press right HERE on this inscription and see what pops out!

Now, the audience should know that Penelope is just BESIDE herself with anticipation! A secret compartment in a mysterious manor house? Why, this could lead straight to the legendary Doily Diamond! And that dear Mr. Clyde's nose might have done half the work for her — bless his heart and his FACE!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: AH-HA! I can FEEL it, Miss Pitstop — there's a loose stone here where that click sounded!
